module.subdomain_takeover.checks: For each subdomain found, looks for an alias (CNAME) to an abandoned third-party service that anyone could claim.
module.subdomain_takeover.fix:
For each subdomain flagged: first delete the dangling DNS record (CNAME, or A/AAAA) from the zone, at your DNS host or registrar; this is what closes the exposure right away.
If it must stay in service: recreate the expected resource (site, application, bucket, space) at the third-party provider from YOUR account, with exactly the name the CNAME points to, and attach the custom domain to it; enable domain ownership verification when the provider offers it (TXT record).
"To check" finding: open the name in a browser. The provider's "site not found" page, or a resource-not-found error, is handled as a possible takeover; if you recognize your own content, the CNAME is sound.
List all CNAME records of the zone (zone export) and check that each target still exists and belongs to you (`dig +short CNAME`, then resolve the target); delete those whose target is gone.
Remember the order: before terminating a third-party service (site, hosting, bucket, free trial), delete its DNS record, never the other way round.
If the subdomain may have been taken over: consider it compromised, check the certificates issued for that name, invalidate sessions and cookies carried by the parent domain, and check that no service (OAuth redirects, CORS, CSP, SPF) still trusts that name.
Check with the commands in the snippet: `dig +short CNAME` must return nothing for the deleted name, and the target of a kept CNAME must not answer `NXDOMAIN`; then run the scan again.
module.subdomain_takeover.fix_snippet:
# Bash
dig +short CNAME app.example.com
dig app-old.example.net | grep "status:"
curl -sI --max-time 10 https://app.example.com

# PowerShell
Resolve-DnsName app.example.com -Type CNAME
Resolve-DnsName app-old.example.net
module.subdomain_takeover.title: Subdomain takeover
module.subdomain_takeover.why: A hijacked subdomain serves the attacker's content under the victim's name: credible phishing, cookie theft, brand damage.
